key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks discover strongly nonlinear water waves, with one candidate independently certified by interval arithmetic and a Lean-checked residual theorem.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to auditable, high-accuracy computations of nonlinear free-surface flows.
method: Learn periodic wave profiles, speed and optionally surface tension from governing equations without training data.
Use staged training and refinement to reach near-machine-precision equation residuals.
Freeze one candidate, bound its continuum residual with interval arithmetic, and formalize the certification deductions in Lean.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples, plus new high-amplitude candidates from continuation and a rigorous uniform residual bound for one candidate.
watch_item: A certified small residual does not by itself establish proximity to an exact solution, physical stability or generalization to other flow regimes.
paper_title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
